# claude-pool

> claude-pool is a single-file, zero-dependency Node.js (18+) tool that pools several Claude subscriptions (Pro / Max) for Claude Code. When the account a session runs on hits its 5-hour or weekly usage limit, it switches to the account with the most headroom and resumes the same conversation with `claude --resume <id>`. On Windows it adds a transparent desktop widget with every account's limits, one-click login buttons (private browser window, token captured automatically), a background daemon that starts with Windows, and "auto hi": a 1-token message right after each 5h reset so the next window starts at once.

Use it when Claude Code keeps stopping with "usage limit reached" and you have more than one Claude subscription, when you want to see all accounts' 5h / 7d limits at a glance, or when you want new terminals to start on whichever account still has capacity.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/shakeebshaan/claude-pool/blob/main/README.md): install, widget, one-click login, auto hi, live switching, commands, configuration, security, FAQ
- [Source](https://github.com/shakeebshaan/claude-pool/blob/main/claude-pool.js): the whole tool in one file; `node claude-pool.js help` prints the usage
- [Tests](https://github.com/shakeebshaan/claude-pool/blob/main/test/widget.test.js): `node --test test/widget.test.js`
- [Agent notes](https://github.com/shakeebshaan/claude-pool/blob/main/AGENTS.md): how to work on the code

## Quick facts

- Install: `node claude-pool.js install` (writes the `cpool` command), then `cpool background on` on Windows
- Run Claude Code with live account switching: `cpool [any claude arguments]`, or `cpool shim on` (Windows) so plain `claude` does the same
- See all limits: `cpool limits`
- Add an account: widget "Log in" / "+ Add account", or `cpool login <name>`, or `claude setup-token` + `cpool add <name>`
- Limits are read from the `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-{5h,7d}-{utilization,reset}` headers of a 1-token Haiku request
- Tokens live in `~/.claude-pool/accounts.json` (owner-only), are never printed, and never appear in the widget data
- Each account keeps its own limits; claude-pool only chooses which of your accounts to use
